title: Exceptions from a static block
answer: A static block may execute code that throws an unchecked exception. If class initialization fails, the JVM wraps the failure in `ExceptionInInitializerError` for the triggering use, and the class is not successfully initialized. Later uses can fail with `NoClassDefFoundError`. Static initialization should therefore avoid fragile operations and should not depend on recoverable external resources whenever simpler lazy initialization is possible.
